name: Ice Spice
label: 10K Projects / Capitol
lede: Ice Spice made six songs in 13 minutes, landed at No. 32 on Pitchfork's 2023 list, and spent the rest of that year on Taylor Swift's and Nicki Minaj's records. A year earlier she was a Bronx student with a Wendy's name tag.

eras.title: Isis from the Bronx
eras.text: Isis Gaston grew up on hip-hop in the Bronx, started a fake Instagram account at 14 and left college in her sophomore year. Then she met a producer who shared her campus and her taste.

years.h: Isis Naija Gaston is born in the Bronx
years.p: Her father, Joseph Gaston, is an underground rapper. Her mother, Charina Almanzar, is Dominican and was 17 at the birth.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia, her parents met at a McDonald's and divorced when she was two. She started on Lil' Kim and Nicki Minaj at age 7, and her father's record collection added Jay-Z, 50 Cent and Wu-Tang Clan. At 14 she made a fake Instagram account called Ice Spice and kept the name when she started rapping.

years.h: Gaston plays defensive specialist at SUNY Purchase and works the Wendy's register
years.p: She graduated from Sacred Heart High School in Yonkers, then enrolled at SUNY Purchase and joined the volleyball team.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists her 2018 season as 2 kills and 9 digs. She studied communications, worked as a cashier at Wendy's and The Gap, and left school in her sophomore year, citing the commute.

years.h: "Bully Freestyle" is her first song, made with [[RiotUSA|f0efd347-c9ae-4bd8-8646-4559f4feb360]]
years.p: Ephrem Lopez Jr., a Bronx-raised communications major at Purchase, produced it. Ice Spice had just gone viral for a "Buss It" challenge video.
years.xp: Wikipedia's RiotUSA page says the pair met at Purchase in 2021 and that he produced "Bully Freestyle" that March. Its Ice Spice page dates their first work to 2020, so the order of those two events is a small conflict between the pages. Every major Ice Spice song since has had his name on it.

eras.title: Weeks from meme to major label
eras.text: One short, sticky song shot around the Bronx got her a Drake co-sign, a meme and a record deal in a matter of weeks.

years.cap: Ice Spice on stage at Outernet, London, November 4, 2024
years.p: RiotUSA produced it, and Ice Spice posted a screenshot showing Drake had co-signed it. The video, shot around the Bronx, turned into a meme.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says the video, directed by George Buford, has her dancing at a park, in front of Paya Deli and at a photoshoot. The song reached No. 5 on Billboard's Bubbling Under Hot 100 and is RIAA platinum.

GRAMMY.com put it at nearly 120 million Spotify streams while it was still an independent release.

years.h: A major-label deal arrives weeks after the video
years.p: 10K Projects and Capitol Records sign her in September 2022, and both names are on every release since.
years.xp: GRAMMY.com says the record deal with 10K Projects and Capitol Records followed shortly after the video became a meme. The label name on everything since, including her 2023 EP, is 10K Projects / Capitol.

eras.title: Like..? and the year she was on everyone's record
eras.text: The six-song EP became the one critics kept talking about, and Ice Spice spent the rest of the year on other people's hits: PinkPantheress, Nicki Minaj, Taylor Swift and Barbie.

years.h: Pitchfork gives Like..? a 7.6 and ranks it 32nd of 2023
years.p: RiotUSA executive produced all six songs, including "Munch" and "Bikini Bottom." The standard edition runs 13 minutes.
years.xp:
The standard edition runs 13 minutes and 8 seconds. Metacritic's average is 69 from six reviews, and HipHopDX gave it 4.1 out of 5. Pitchfork's list blurb, quoted by AlbumOfTheYear, praises her "filthy, laugh-out-loud punchlines."

Other year-end placings listed on Wikipedia: No. 3 at The New York Times, No. 6 at the Los Angeles Times, No. 18 at Billboard, No. 21 at Slant and No. 52 at Rolling Stone. It debuted at No. 37 on the Billboard 200 and later peaked at No. 15. A deluxe edition followed on July 21, 2023.

years.h: [[PinkPantheress|7441014f-f8f5-494f-81db-ff166fbc078d]] pulls her into the Hot 100 top three
years.p: "Boy's a liar Pt. 2" reaches No. 3, her first top-three entry.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the single to February 3, 2023. It was the first of four songs that took her to the top ten that year.

years.cap: Ice Spice at the iHeartRadio Music Awards, April 2024
years.h: Nicki Minaj answers the shout-out with a "Princess Diana" remix
years.p: Ice Spice had called Minaj "my idol" at Rolling Loud California that March. The remix reached No. 4 on the Hot 100.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, Minaj answered the Rolling Loud shout-out on Instagram and the two teased the remix on social media before April 14. It was the first release on Minaj's own label, Heavy on It, and it went to No. 1 on US Rhythmic Airplay.

years.cap: Ice Spice performing at Outernet, London, November 4, 2024
yt: Taylor Swift, Karma (feat. Ice Spice) video
years.h: Taylor Swift puts an Ice Spice verse on "Karma"
years.p: Swift said Ice Spice's team reached out, and that she then contacted Ice Spice herself. They played it live at the Eras Tour show in East Rutherford, N.J., the day it came out.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, the remix was announced May 24 and released May 26 as part of a digital-only Til Dawn Edition of Midnights. It peaked at No. 2 on the Hot 100, her highest-charting single.

Pitchfork's Shaad D'Souza called the pairing a "clash of sensibilities," according to Wikipedia. It was nominated for Best Pop Duo/Group Performance at the 2024 Grammys.

yt: Barbie World (with Aqua), Barbie The Album
years.h: Aqua's "Barbie Girl" gets the Minaj and Ice Spice treatment
years.p: "Barbie World" debuts at No. 7 and credits Aqua's members as songwriters alongside Minaj, Ice Spice and RiotUSA.
years.xp: Wikipedia notes the No. 7 debut matched the peak of the original "Barbie Girl." Hannah Lux Davis directed the video, set in a Barbie Dreamhouse. The song earned two Grammy nominations.

years.big: Everybody was tryna be like, 'Oh, she a one-hit wonder'
q: Everybody was tryna be like, 'Oh, she a one-hit wonder'
yt: BET Awards medley: Munch, Princess Diana, In Ha Mood
years.h: She ends 2023 with four Hot 100 top-ten songs
years.p: The peaks were 3, 4, 2 and 7, for "Boy's a liar Pt. 2," "Princess Diana," "Karma" and "Barbie World." She also won Best New Artist at the MTV VMAs.
years.xp: GRAMMY.com quotes Ice Spice on the skeptics who said she was a one-hit wonder after "Munch." Wikipedia credits her as the only rapper with four Hot 100 top-ten songs in 2023.

eras.title: From Grammy night to the big screen
eras.text: The Grammy nominations came first, then her first full album and a London show at Outernet. Acting followed.

years.cap: Ice Spice performing at Outernet, London, November 4, 2024
years.src: GRAMMY.com · E! News: Grammys mistakenly · E! News: Victoria Monét
years.h: The Recording Academy posts the wrong Best Rap Song winner
years.p: Ice Spice was up for Best New Artist, and for "Karma" and "Barbie World" with Swift and Minaj. Victoria Monét won Best New Artist.
years.xp: E! News reported that the Recording Academy briefly posted "Barbie World" as the Best Rap Song winner on social media, then deleted it and replaced it with the real winner, Killer Mike's "Scientists & Engineers."

years.h: Her first full album, Y2K!, opens at No. 18
years.p: It sold 28,000 equivalent units in week one on the Billboard 200, with Travis Scott, Gunna and Central Cee as guests.
years.xp: Wikipedia puts Metacritic at 65 from 17 reviews. The Guardian's Alexis Petridis called it "wilfully trashy, brief and throwaway," and also "fun while it lasts." Production came from RiotUSA, Goldin, Synthetic and Upmadeit. A deluxe edition followed on December 25, 2024.

years.cap: Ice Spice at the Vetements Spring/Summer 2026 show, Paris, October 2025
years.p: She played Marisol Cepeda in the film, then voiced a ticket taker in The SpongeBob Movie: Search for SquarePants.
